title: Incubation system to assess gaseous emissions from environmental samples under controlled conditions
author: Agostini, Krause, et al.
materials: Gas scrubbers were filled with 30 mL 0.08 M sulfuric acid (H2SO4) each. The H2SO4 concentration was chosen according to the maximum amount of NH3 estimated to be emitted during the scrubbing period with an overhead of 100 % to account for the large uncertainty in estimation of NH3 volatilization. Initial and final NH4—N concentrations in the sample bottles and the NH4—N concentration in gas scrubber 1 were quantified performing the Berthelot reaction [9] followed by spectrophotometry (Genesys 150 UV–Vis, Thermo Fischer Scientific, USA).

steps.title: Assemble ISAGE incubation system
steps.instruction: Build 24 ISAGE units using 250 mL screw‑top bottles with GL 45 caps modified to have an inlet, outlet and sampling port. Install Discofix® C valves (Braun) on each cap to close inlet/outlet for the non‑steady‑state configuration. Connect all components with 4 mm‑ID PTFE tubing. Insert two 50 mL gas scrubbers between each bottle outlet and the vacuum generator. Use a single‑stage venturi valve (VN‑05‑N‑T3‑PQ2‑VQ2‑RQ2, Festo) powered by compressed air at ~40 psi to generate flow, adding orifice restrictors and a vacuum reservoir to stabilise pressure. Provide a flow‑control valve for each bottle. Arrange the units in two sets of twelve; each set occupies a 440 mm × 317 mm area on a 12 mm laminated board, held by custom 3D‑printed structures secured with M4 threaded rods and nuts. Each set contains two 2 L vacuum reservoirs and two venturi valves shared among six bottles; a single compressor supplies all units. Place the whole assembly inside an incubator (e.g., TS 606/3, WTW) for temperature control.

steps.title: Prepare acid gas scrubbers
steps.instruction: Fill each gas scrubber (capacity 50 mL) with 30 mL of 0.08 M H₂SO₄. The acid volume provides a 100 % excess capacity to trap all NH₃ emitted during the scrubbing period.

steps.title: Load sample bottles with solution
steps.instruction: Add 100 mL of (NH₄)₂SO₄ aqueous solution at the desired initial NH₄‑N concentration (0, 0.2, 0.5 or 1 g N L⁻¹) to each bottle. Immediately before starting the scrubbing event, add 2 mL of 1 M NaOH to each bottle to raise pH and initiate NH₃ volatilisation (future runs may instead adjust pH to 9 using a variable NaOH volume).

steps.title: Configure inlet/outlet valves for measurement mode
steps.instruction: For non‑steady‑state measurements, close both inlet and outlet valves with the Discofix® C valves and access the headspace through the sampling port via a septum held by an exetainer head. For steady‑state measurements, open the inlet and outlet valves, attach the inlet extension to direct incoming air to the sample surface, and allow air to flow from inlet to outlet through the venturi system.

steps.title: Set headspace turnover rate
steps.instruction: Adjust the flow‑control valve of each bottle so that the gas flow at the bottle inlet equals 213 mL min⁻¹, which corresponds to a headspace turnover rate of 1 min⁻¹ for a 100 mL sample volume in a 250 mL bottle. Verify the flow with a Testo 405i flow meter (4 mm tubing ID); 213 mL min⁻¹ is equivalent to a linear velocity of 0.28 m s⁻¹. Perform this adjustment at the start of every scrubbing event.

steps.title: Run scrubbing event for designated time
steps.instruction: Start the air flow so that headspace gases pass through scrubber 1 (acid) and then scrubber 2 (acid). Maintain the flow for the chosen scrubbing period (1 h, 6 h or 12 h) while keeping the incubator at the selected temperature (15 °C, 20 °C or 25 °C).

steps.title: Terminate volatilisation and collect samples
steps.instruction: At the end of the scrubbing period, stop the air flow and add 0.9 mL of 1 M H₂SO₄ to each bottle to halt further NH₃ emission. Collect an aliquot from each sample bottle for NH₄‑N analysis and withdraw the entire acid solution from scrubber 1 for NH₄‑N measurement.

steps.title: Analyze NH4‑N by Berthelot reaction
steps.instruction: Determine NH₄‑N concentrations in the bottle aliquots and in scrubber 1 solution using the Berthelot reaction followed by spectrophotometric measurement on a Genesys 150 UV‑Vis spectrophotometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific).

steps.title: Calculate NH3 volatilisation fluxes
steps.instruction: Compute the actual NH₃‑N flux with: ActualFlux = (NH₄‑NStart – NH₄‑NEnd) × 100 mL ÷ (0.003 m⁻² × ScrubbingTime). Compute the measured flux with: MeasuredFlux = NH₄‑N_Scrubber1 × 30 mL ÷ (0.003 m⁻² × ScrubbingTime). Use the appropriate scrubbing time (h) for each run.

steps.title: Perform GHG measurement (optional)
steps.instruction: If greenhouse‑gas (GHG) quantification is required, first operate the system in steady‑state mode for at least 1 h to flush the headspace and obtain a low baseline. Then switch to non‑steady‑state mode, add an equivalent volume of an inert gas (e.g., He) to the headspace before each sample withdrawal to equilibrate pressure. Sample the headspace manually into evacuated exetainers or automatically with a Multi‑Purpose‑Sampler (Gerstel) and analyse the gases by gas chromatography: use an electron‑capture detector for N₂O and a flame‑ionisation detector for CO₂ and CH₄.

steps.title: Monitor and correct water loss
steps.instruction: Gravimetrically measure the water mass of each sample before and after each scrubbing event. If water loss exceeds 5 % of the initial water content, add demineralised water to restore the original water mass before the next run.
